timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi everyone, welcome back to our channel. Today we are hiking to the Kaishan Train located near
Yunlong. It's an easy and scenic train at an elevation of 121 meters and 2.1 kilometers.
From Tinshui, via MTR, walk onto Tindford Road. Follow the signs for Hamei San Shun and
continue walking on this path until you arrive at a public restroom and a car park.
A few steps ahead of the car park on the opposite side is the start of the hike.
Walk between the trees until you reach the cleared area soon. Take the steps up from there.
You can already start seeing the skyline option then in the back drop.
Most part of this hike is unshaded. Apart from few benches under the tree, you will be hiking in
the open area. So be careful if you are hiking during summer months and don't forget to carry your
caps, brailers and sunscreen.
You will also notice the trail is very popular for RC enthusiasts of
floating their toys and sometimes also falling sideways too. It was real fun watching how they
were controlled and most of them also made it to the top. Follow this path and you will arrive at
a three way junction. Take the extreme left as this is less steep and easy to climb.
Before you reach the top, take a short break and enjoy the rolling grassy haloks of Kaishan.
Once you reach the top, you will notice the wetlands of Namstangwai as well as the
Shenzhen skyline across the bay. These wetlands of Namstangwai are popularly known for their fish
ponds, ekeleptis trees and also one of the preferred sites by bird watchers.
More on Namstangwai in another video, other major highlights of this hike are the rock paintings
found along the section of the trail. The interesting part is they have used the original structure of
the stones to create a three dimensional effect. These outdoor art pieces are hand painted by locals
and depict scenes of rural life. To complete your hike, follow the paved driveway to Fukshun Street
and locate the Minibus bus stop. Take green minibus number 74 which will bring you to Long Ping
MTR station. We hope you enjoyed our video and found it useful. For more such videos,
subscribe to our channel. Till then, bye bye.

Complete guide to our hike can be found here - https://twistyroutes.com/blog/kai-shan-hike 

Kai Shan (髻山) is a hill in Wang Chau, near Yuen Long in the New Territories of Hong Kong. If you are looking for an easy and scenic hike, this hike is a perfect combination of both.
